## Portable CMake 3.20+ guidance for a C++23 executable

Minimal modern shape:

```cmake
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
project(MyApp LANGUAGES CXX)

add_executable(myapp)

target_sources(myapp
  PRIVATE
    src/main.cpp
    src/foo.cpp
    src/foo.hpp
)

target_include_directories(myapp
  PRIVATE
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src"
)

target_compile_features(myapp PRIVATE cxx_std_23)
set_target_properties(myapp PROPERTIES
  CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF
)
```

### 1. Prefer explicit source lists; glob only with eyes open

**Best practice**: list sources explicitly with `target_sources()`. This makes added/removed files visible in diffs and reliably triggers CMake regeneration.

CMake’s own docs warn against source globbing:

> “We do not recommend using GLOB to collect a list of source files from your source tree…”  
> Evidence: [`Help/command/file.rst#L368-L373`](https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/blob/85e2c275bdb13e5711e69d959259a05f7322f008/Help/command/file.rst#L368-L373)

If you choose globbing for a small hand-written project:

```cmake
file(GLOB CONFIGURE_DEPENDS APP_SOURCES
  "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/*.cpp"
  "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/*.hpp"
)

target_sources(myapp PRIVATE ${APP_SOURCES})
```

Use `CONFIGURE_DEPENDS`, but note CMake says it may not work reliably on all generators and adds rebuild-check cost.

### 2. Use target-local C++23 requirements

Use:

```cmake
target_compile_features(myapp PRIVATE cxx_std_23)
set_target_properties(myapp PROPERTIES CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)
```

CMake 3.20 knows `cxx_std_23`:

> `cxx_std_23` — “Compiler mode is at least C++ 23.”  
> Evidence: [`CMAKE_CXX_KNOWN_FEATURES.rst#L44-L47`](https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/blob/85e2c275bdb13e5711e69d959259a05f7322f008/Help/prop_gbl/CMAKE_CXX_KNOWN_FEATURES.rst#L44-L47)

Disable extensions for portability because `CXX_EXTENSIONS` controls compiler-specific modes like `gnu++11` vs `c++11`:

> Evidence: [`CXX_EXTENSIONS.rst#L6-L13`](https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/blob/85e2c275bdb13e5711e69d959259a05f7322f008/Help/prop_tgt/CXX_EXTENSIONS.rst#L6-L13)

### 3. Keep include dirs target-scoped

For your `src` include directory:

```cmake
target_include_directories(myapp
  PRIVATE
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src"
)
```

Avoid global `include_directories()`. Target-scoped properties are more portable and avoid leaking include paths into unrelated targets.

### 4. Output directory behavior: usually leave default

By default, CMake puts runtime artifacts in generator/build-tree-specific locations. That is usually best for portability, especially with Visual Studio/Xcode/Ninja Multi-Config.

Only set output directories if you really need a stable local layout:

```cmake
set_target_properties(myapp PROPERTIES
  RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/bin"
)
```

CMake documents `RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY` as the directory where runtime target files are built:

> Evidence: [`XXX_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY.rst#L1-L4`](https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/blob/85e2c275bdb13e5711e69d959259a05f7322f008/Help/prop_tgt/include/XXX_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY.rst#L1-L4)

For multi-config generators, CMake may append a per-configuration subdirectory unless a generator expression is used:

> Evidence: [`XXX_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY.rst#L6-L9`](https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/blob/85e2c275bdb13e5711e69d959259a05f7322f008/Help/prop_tgt/include/XXX_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY.rst#L6-L9)

If you need config-specific dirs:

```cmake
set_target_properties(myapp PROPERTIES
  RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY_DEBUG   "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/bin/Debug"
  RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY_RELEASE "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/bin/Release"
)
```

### 5. Threads: link `Threads::Threads` when code uses threading

If the executable uses `<thread>`, pthread APIs, or platform thread support, use:

set(THREADS_PREFER_PTHREAD_FLAG TRUE)

For C++23, do **not** add `stdc++fs` or `c++fs` by default. Those were transitional needs for older GCC/libstdc++ or older libc++ setups. With a CMake 3.20+ / C++23-oriented build, require a modern compiler instead.
